title: Storm lightning flashes independently per display instead of one strike across all screens

title: ow-wgt resolution: Codex-flagged fixes (hot-plug, stale-storm, real-weather tests, JS envelope, reduced-motion)
description:
Codex blind review of ow-wgt (lightning) found 4 issues to fix. All rendering logic stays unchanged; only correctness and test gaps are addressed.

FIX 1: HOT-PLUG storm state lost. WebWallpaperView.latestStorm starts false; didFinish always calls applyStormNow(latestStorm=false) which unregisters the effect for monitors added during an active storm. Fix: initialize latestStorm from initialStorm in init so newcomers keep the correct current storm state.

FIX 2: Stale weather must not keep lightning active. computeAndBroadcast derives stormActive from effectiveWeatherCode even when resolveWeather returned nil (stale cache >21600s or fetch failed). Fix: stormActive=false whenever resolveWeather returns nil. OW_WGT_TEST force-active path stays as-is. Add selftest: nil weather + effectiveCode=95 => stormActive false.

FIX 3: Real weather trigger test. lightning-check.sh only exercises OW_WGT_TEST forced hook. Add sub-checks (c) storm fixture (weather_code 95) via OW_MOOD_FAKE_RESPONSE_FILE => assert active=true effect=registered on every window; (d) clear fixture (code 0) => active=false effect=none.

FIX 4a: JS envelope readback. Expose window.__wgtFlashAlpha(elapsedMs, peak) in wallpaper.js. Add lightning-check sub-check that calls it via evaluateJavaScript readback at t=0, t=10, t=20, t=21, t=140 and asserts rise/peak/decay/zero shape.

FIX 4b: Reduced motion guard. Add OW_WGT_REDUCED_MOTION=1 env -> native injects window.__wgtReducedMotion=true at document-start. wallpaper.js applyStorm checks it in addition to matchMedia. Add lightning-check sub-check: storm ACTIVE + OW_WGT_REDUCED_MOTION=1 => effect=none.

title: Multi-display slice sync + pause/resume when displays are on different Spaces
description: Surfaced during the ow-94b.5 web-video de-risk (observed by Anoop on macOS 26.5.2). The spanned canvas (DEC-002) is one screen-sized WKWebView window PER display, each showing a slice of one oversized stage, with an independent video decode per screen (see known-limitations). Observed per-window behavior: a display whose desktop Space is visible keeps animating; a display taken into a full-screen app Space has its wallpaper slice PAUSED (occlusion/Space culling) and RESUMES when returning to the desktop Space (not frozen). OPEN QUESTIONS for the spanned design: (1) When one display is in a full-screen Space while the other stays on the desktop, does the still-visible slice keep animating (expected yes) and does the hidden slice pause independently (expected yes)? (2) CRITICAL: when the paused slice resumes, is it FRAME-SYNCED with the other slice, or does it drift, breaking the continuous-across-the-bezel image? Investigate a shared playback clock / periodic resync (e.g. seek both <video> elements to a common wall-clock-derived time) so slices stay aligned across pause/resume and across independent decodes. Reuse the ow-94b.5 telemetry (currentTime per window) to measure drift.
design:
# FINAL plan: ow-blz.5 (video sync) + ow-blz.6 (lightning sync)

Session tuple owned natively by WallpaperController: (epochMs, sourceRev, durationSec, seed).
- epochMs: wall clock ms when the current source started. durationSec: probed natively
  (AVURLAsset) once per source and shared, never per-element video.duration. seed: random
  uint32 per app run (fixed in test mode). sourceRev bumps on Choose video.
- Injected at document start (WKUserScript, like __wallpaper geometry) for every view incl.
  hot-plug newcomers; survivors get a runtime apply ONLY if the tuple changed. Choose video is
  ONE JS call per view that sets the new src and the new session together.

Video (wallpaper.js + index.html):
- Remove `autoplay` and `loop` from the <video>. The sync controller is the only code that
  calls play() and the only author of the wrap. Existing autoplay/tryPlay paths must not start
  playback independently (they may only defer to the controller).
- target = ((Date.now() - epochMs)/1000) mod durationSec. err = presented - target wrapped to
  [-d/2, d/2]; presented = requestVideoFrameCallback mediaTime (fallback currentTime).
- Join (loadedmetadata, playing, visibilitychange to visible, rev change): seek to target,
  play, and after 'seeked' re-check once; re-seek if |err| > 2 frames.
- Every ~1 s: |err| > 2 frames -> re-seek; half a frame < |err| <= 2 frames -> playbackRate
  1 -/+ up to 0.01 proportional; else rate 1.0. Never outside [0.99, 1.01].
- Wrap: when target wraps past the end, seek to the wrapped time (all windows do this at the
  same wall-clock instant). Ignore stale events whose rev differs.

Lightning (ow-blz.6):
- Stateless pure function of (seed, Date.now()): slot = floor(now/slotMs); hash(seed, slot)
  decides burst presence, start offset, origin in UNION STAGE POINTS (__wallpaper.stageW/H),
  peak, flicker count and gaps; alpha = envelope(now - start). Convert origin to backing pixels
  only when drawing. No Math.random and no rAF ts on the scheduling/envelope path. Re-register
  or resume just recomputes the phase.

Gate scripts/sync-check.sh (OW_SYNC_TEST), real WKWebViews, real generated clip (ffmpeg, 30fps,
short GOP, about 4 s so the seam is crossed several times):
- FAIL if fewer than 2 wallpaper windows.
- Per window every 250 ms JS logs: rev, epochMs, durationSec, Date.now, rVFC mediaTime,
  currentTime, playbackRate, paused. Compare the per-window (presented - target) offsets.
- Assert steady-state max pairwise offset <= max(1 frame, 20 ms), including samples across
  seams; forced desync hook (+2 s on one window) reconverges within 1.5 s; falsifiability hook
  (constant +80 ms offset on one window) MUST fail; video swap converges on the new rev;
  rebuild (existing rebuild/fake-screens hook) keeps alignment.
- Lightning: fixed seed and short slots in test mode; every window logs identical event
  records (JSON identity: id, start, origin in stage points, flicker sequence); plus one pixel
  readback during a known flash window via the existing overlay readback path.
- JS unit-style check of the pure lightning function with frozen timestamps.

Out of scope: Space pause/resume is Phase 5 manual; rain stays per window.
acceptance_criteria: The spanned wallpaper keeps a single continuous image across displays: every display presents the same video frame (presented-frame media time via requestVideoFrameCallback; currentTime is unreliable in WebKit, it freezes after ended and jitters 40 to 90 ms) within max(1 frame, 20 ms) in steady state, across loop seams, after video swap, reload and hot-plug, verified by scripts/sync-check.sh on every connected display. Space pause/resume realignment is verified manually in Phase 5 (Spaces cannot be driven by automation); the controller's 250 ms tick realigns a resumed window regardless of visibilitychange.
notes: 2026-10-18 user report (verbatim): 'in the animated videos, the videos across multiple screens are actually out of sync... when the lightning flashes, it's supposed to be across all three screens. The video itself has lightning... it's coming at different timing across all three. And video itself is playing three different parts, like three different timestamps of the same video.' Must ship before the next release (blocks ow-t4r.5).

title: De-risk WKWebView video rendering continuously at desktop level on Tahoe
description: The ow-mbw.1 spike de-risks an AppKit + CoreAnimation desktop-level window, but the product render path (DEC-001) is a looping <video> inside a transparent WKWebView, which uses a different compositor path (IOSurface / render-server) that macOS has historically throttled independently. A green AppKit/CA spike does NOT prove the real wallpaper keeps animating. This task validates: a muted+playsinline looping <video> in a transparent WKWebView, pinned at CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow), keeps decoding and compositing new frames continuously on macOS 26 (behind icons, click-through, all Spaces, and crucially after >=2 minutes with another app frontmost, i.e. not frozen by occlusion or App Nap). Reuse the validated window factory from ow-mbw.1.
design: Throwaway env-gated (OW_WEBSPIKE=1) WebKit de-risk, mutually exclusive with OW_SPIKE. NEW WebSpikeWindow.swift (only file allowed WKWebView): copies the measured ow-mbw.1 window property table (NOT makeSpikeWindow) with isOpaque=false + backgroundColor=.clear; WKWebViewConfiguration.mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback=[] (NOT allowsInlineMediaPlayback, iOS-only); transparency via underPageBackgroundColor=.clear + CSS (NO drawsBackground KVC, private); loadFileURL(allowingReadAccessTo:); telemetry via WKScriptMessageHandler; polls WKMediaPlaybackState; logs webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate; enumerates PID-owned on-screen windows and flags any layer >= desktop-icon level. Throwaway web/webspike/{index.html,style.css,app.js}: full-bleed muted playsinline loop autoplay video, no controls, disablepictureinpicture, disableremoteplayback, filter: brightness(1.01) (DEC-001 chose WKWebView FOR filters; a filter forces the freezable backing-store recomposite, so test WITH a filter). Oracle: machine-readable COLOR BLOCK driven by frame# burned into the VIDEO (not a JS HUD) in a known center-fraction crop; RVFC presented-frame counter; postMessage telemetry only. Asset: ffmpeg H.264 yuv420p 1920x1080@30, 17.3s (non-divisor of 120), -an (NO audio: a silent track can hold a media power assertion that masks App Nap), color-block + human digits, generated into .build/webspike/ (NOT in-tree).
acceptance_criteria: A transparent WKWebView desktop-layer window shows a continuously playing video behind icons that is still advancing after a >=2 minute occluded watch on AC power.
notes: PASS with benign occlusion nuance. The WKWebView <video> at the desktop layer keeps presenting frames continuously whenever its Space is visible: WebKit does NOT throttle the hidden/occluded page (RVFC presentedFrames advance with document.visibilityState=hidden, media=playing for 125s, no WebContent termination). Proven on glass by screencapture -l showing the burned-in counter advancing. Direct Phase 5 observation (Anoop): visible wallpaper animates (incl. behind a same-Space maximized window); a display taken into its own full-screen Space pauses (macOS occlusion/Space culling) and RESUMES live on return (not frozen). So screencapture -l of a 100%-occluded window is not a freeze oracle (it measures compositor culling); the authoritative liveness signals are RVFC + media=playing + a VISIBLE window animating, all of which passed. 4 cold Codex passes; final adjudication: transparency gating REJECTED (by design, a reported finding for ow-94b.1); z-order actual-layer assert + OW_WEBSPIKE_ACTIVITY env hygiene FIXED; per-window-telemetry-id, cmp-byte-diff, and foreground-app-assertion documented as known throwaway-check limitations (authoritative oracle is direct observation + per-window pixel gate + RVFC). Follow-ups: multi-display slice sync across pause/resume (ow-blz.5); true idle App Nap not exercised (ow-aad.1). Findings: ow-local/systems/web-render/webview-video-spike-findings.md.
close_reason: De-risk PASS: a looping, filtered, muted <video> in a transparent WKWebView at the desktop window level keeps presenting frames continuously on Tahoe whenever its Space is visible (WebKit does not throttle the occluded/hidden page; RVFC + media=playing sustained 125s; proven on glass). Fully-hidden windows pause via macOS occlusion culling and resume live (benign). Validated by direct observation + automated gates. Seeds ow-94b.1. Follow-ups: ow-blz.5 (slice sync), ow-aad.1 (idle App Nap).

title: Rebuild on display hot-plug / arrangement change
description: Observe NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification; tear down and rebuild all windows with recomputed geometry.
design:
FINAL (Opus + Codex co-scope + Grok red-team; Grok's 11 objections ALL ACCEPTED, a redesign from candidate-recreation to IN-PLACE update).
WHY NOT RECREATE: a new WKWebView hidden behind the old one has its WindowServer backing store culled (ow-94b.5), so revealing it shows the opaque black base for >=1 composite = black flash; also restarts video at t=0 on every nudge. REJECTED.
ARCHITECTURE (in-place):
1. Observe NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification (main actor, resnapshot NSScreen.screens, ignore userInfo) + NSWorkspace screensDidWakeNotification; both call one scheduleRefresh(). Do NOT rebuild on sleep. (Phase 5 must verify the notification even fires for our LSUIElement/accessory app on hot-plug; if missed, add CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback as a debounce-only kick, still snapshotting NSScreen.)
2. Coalesce ~0.3-0.5s, latest snapshot wins.
3. EMPTY-CONFIRM (critical, fixes a daily sleep/wake blank): an empty snapshot NEVER commits on first look; arm a 1-2s confirm timer; commit empty only if still empty when it fires; any non-empty cancels; generation-guard the callback.
4. NO-OP via pure arrangementChanged(old,new) over descriptors {displayID, frame(points), backingScaleFactor, pixel size}. displayID is identity; never match on the ?? 0 fallback.

title: SwiftPM package skeleton + app lifecycle
description: Package.swift (executable), main.swift, AppDelegate. NSApplication with .accessory activation policy (no Dock icon, no Info.plist). App launches and stays running.
design: Target: single executableTarget OnlyWallpapers at Sources/OnlyWallpapers (main.swift + AppDelegate.swift). Package.swift: swift-tools-version 6.2, platforms [.macOS(.v14)], swiftSettings [.defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)]. No Info.plist, no resources, no second target (if empty web/ trips a SwiftPM unhandled-files warning, exclude web for now; ow-94b.3 converts it to a Bundle.module resource). main.swift: plain top-level code (NSApplication.shared, retain delegate as top-level let, assign, app.run()); no @MainActor annotation and no withExtendedLifetime (defaultIsolation covers actor isolation, top-level let covers lifetime). AppDelegate: final NSObject + NSApplicationDelegate; set NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory) in applicationWillFinishLaunching (canonical pre-window hook, avoids Dock flicker) and precondition its Bool return; emit a stdout ready line including the runtime policy. scripts/smoke-run.sh is the behavioral quality gate.

title: Adaptive ambient mood: time-of-day + live weather driven tint/effects
description:
User idea (Anoop): the wallpaper's tone and effects adapt to time of day AND live weather. Example: cloudy/stormy days get a matching mood (desaturated/cooler tint + rain overlay); clear days brighter/warmer; night cooler/dimmer. Extends ow-aqx.1 (time-of-day mood) with weather.
ARCHITECTURE (fits the native-detects / web-renders split): native fetches time + weather, maps to an effect PROFILE, injects it; the web layer renders via (a) a CSS filter on #bg for tint/brightness/saturation (the validated recomposite path - hue-rotate/brightness/saturate/sepia, NO transform) and (b) the #overlay canvas (ow-aqx.3) for particles (rain streaks, snow, fog veil, occasional lightning flash).
WEATHER SOURCE: Open-Meteo (free, NO API key, NO auth, returns current conditions + WMO weather code + cloud cover + precipitation by lat/lon) is the pragmatic choice. (Apple WeatherKit is the native option but needs a Developer Team key/entitlement + a signed app - too heavy for an unsigned local app.) Map the WMO code to a profile: clear / partly-cloudy / overcast / rain / storm / snow / fog.
LOCATION (the key decision): options are CoreLocation (precise, but a permission prompt for an accessory/LSUIElement app), coarse IP-geolocation (automatic, no prompt, city-level - good enough for weather), or a user-configured city/lat-lon in config.json (no prompt, manual). 
TIME-OF-DAY base (ow-aqx.1): a continuous tint curve - warm sunrise, neutral midday, warm sunset, cool/dim night - from the local clock (+ sunrise/sunset from Open-Meteo for accuracy). Weather modulates on top.
CADENCE: refresh weather every ~15-30 min (cache); update the time curve every few min. Fail gracefully: no network -> time-of-day only, no weather, no crash.
PRIVACY/NETWORK (flag): the app is currently 100% OFFLINE; this makes it make a network call (weather API + maybe IP-geo). Make it OPT-IN / configurable, document it. DEPENDS on ow-aqx.1 (tint base) + ow-aqx.3 (overlay for particles). This likely becomes the umbrella that ow-aqx.1 feeds into.
design:
FINAL Stage-1 design (Opus+Codex+Grok, all objections adjudicated). Plan file: /tmp/ow-consensus-plan.md.

GROK RED-TEAM ADJUDICATION (every objection explicit):
- Obj1 Timezone/DST/clock mixing (HIGH): ACCEPT. Open-Meteo naive strings vs Mac Date() = Bangalore bug again. Fix: timeformat=unixtime, parse sunrise/sunset/time as epoch seconds (absolute instants), recompute phase each tick, polar guard (no divide-by-zero). REJECT only the self-computed NOAA solar model (scope creep; we already fetch sunrise/sunset).
- Obj2 Filter mapping (HIGH): ACCEPT. Pin hue-rotate at 0 (wheel-spin, not temperature); warm=small sepia<=0.12, cool=lower saturate+brightness; clamps tighten B[0.85,1.08] S[0.7,1.15] Se[0,0.12]; hold contrast>=1.01 as live-floor (never pure identity, protects ow-94b.5 recomposite path); pass cloud_cover+precipitation into the map (the users cloudy/stormy signal); weather = additive offsets on time profile.
- Obj3 CoreLocation in accessory app (HIGH): ACCEPT. Location becomes a menu-bar opt-in click (NSApp.activate + requestWhenInUseAuthorization, like the video picker), NOT launch auto-request; ship BOTH NSLocationUsageDescription + NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription; kCLLocationAccuracyKilometer + round lat/lon 2dp; one-shot requestLocation, re-request on wake + ~6h; do NOT construct CLLocationManager if usage key absent (swift run/gates); SHIP config.json lat/lon fallback in Stage 1 (real Bangalore fix if TCC fails); broadcast via WallpaperController.applyMoodToAll + WebWallpaperView.initialMood (mirror framing), not a separate object touching private records.
- Obj4 Refresh jumps vs CSS transition (HIGH): ACCEPT. CSS default #bg becomes the same 5-tuple so interpolation works; transition:none on first apply then enable transition: filter 2s ease (filter prop only, not shorthand); hot-plug newcomers inject current mood document-start, transition off until first paint; weather-group hysteresis (sticky until 2 disagreeing fetches); wake observer not foreground. Animated filter on N layers is a Phase 5 must-watch, NOT pre-validated by ow-94b.5 (that was static).
- Obj5 Testability + config clobber (HIGH): ACCEPT. Test numeric (B,S,C,H,Se) tuple w/ epsilon + frozen UTC epochs (TZ-independent), not WebKit reserialized string; cover polar/nil-weather/clamps + one test cssFilter emits 5 names in order. PREREQ fix: AppStorageManager config I/O becomes MERGE-based so writeFraming preserves lat/lon/weatherCache. Gate reads window.__moodApplied + inline bg.style.filter (not getComputedStyle mid-transition); OW_MOOD_TEST disables location+URLSession, asserts zero api.open-meteo.com.
- Obj6 Privacy/network (MED): ACCEPT. Default time-only until opt-in; rounded km coords; apply-TTL ~6h then time-only+log mood=stale; User-Agent+backoff; log src=location|config|time weather=ok|fail|cache age; keep live network off smoke-run/package-check; README documents network use.

STEP 0 prereq: config.json merge-based. STEP 1 MoodController (opt-in location, Open-Meteo unixtime, cache). STEP 2 pure moodParams+cssFilter + OW_SELFTEST. STEP 3 web applyMood + 5-tuple CSS default + 2s transition + initialMood. STEP 4 package-app.sh both plist keys. STEP 5 scripts/mood-check.sh gate.

title: Reveal animation when the wallpaper comes into view (Space switch / full-screen close)
description: User idea (Anoop): a flash/slide/fade when the wallpaper slides into view - returning from a full-screen app Space to the desktop Space, or when an app Space is closed. FEASIBILITY: doable but fiddly. Signals: NSWindow occlusionState / windowDidChangeOcclusionState, and NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification. On becoming visible, trigger a CSS reveal animation (fade/pulse/slide) in the web layer. This OVERLAPS ow-aad.4 (the transient real-wallpaper reveal during those exact transitions): a reveal animation could mask/soften that beat-late flash (aad.4's freeze-frame idea is the deeper fix). CAVEATS: detecting 'came into view' reliably is the hard part (occlusion signals can be noisy); must not fire on every minor occlusion change; coordinate so all screens animate together.

title: Mouse-reactive effects: cursor halo/spotlight + tint shift
description: User idea (Anoop): the wallpaper reacts to the mouse - a halo/spotlight that follows the cursor, and/or a tint shift near it. FEASIBILITY: doable. The wallpaper window is ignoresMouseEvents=true (click-through), so the WKWebView does NOT get mouse events directly. Use a native GLOBAL mouse monitor (NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents matching .mouseMoved - works for an accessory app; mouse-location monitoring does NOT need Accessibility permission, unlike keyboard/CGEvent taps), map the global mouse point into UNION space, and feed it to the web layer (throttled, e.g. via a lightweight evaluateJavaScript or a shared value + rAF) so the #overlay canvas draws a radial-gradient spotlight/halo at that point. The spotlight appears on whichever screen the mouse is on (one union canvas, sliced). DEPENDS on ow-aqx.3 (wiring the overlay canvas). CAVEATS: throttle hard (do not push 60fps evaluateJavaScript to N webviews - coalesce, skip when idle); the effect sits BEHIND desktop icons (the wallpaper layer), so it reads on empty desktop / gaps; keep it subtle; respect the no-transform-on-video lesson (the overlay is a sibling canvas, safe).

title: Framing controls: object-position reposition (vertical/horizontal) + zoom/scale
description: User (Anoop) wants to control the framing of the cover-cropped video. On the dual-4K span a 16:9 clip is cover-fit to the union, so top/bottom (or sides) get cropped; today you cannot choose WHICH band shows, and the interesting content can be chopped off (observed: bottom of 'midnight-fuel-stop' cut off, wanted to shift it down). Add: (1) object-position reposition (vertical and horizontal) so the user can pan the crop (CSS object-position on #bg, or an equivalent translate within #stage), and (2) a zoom/scale control (scale the video up within the cover frame). Per-wallpaper setting, persisted, and exposed via the menu-bar controls (ow-aqx.7). Interacts with the union-space cover crop (see known-limitations) and the spanning geometry (ow-blz.2); must stay continuous across the bezel. Keep the hardware video layer intact (do not apply a transform to the video PARENT; a transform on #bg itself or object-position is fine).
design:
FINAL (Opus + lean Codex co-scope + Grok red-team; Grok's objections ACCEPTED, notably the pan-formula flaw).
RENDER (no transform): REPOSITION via object-position AND zoom-slack offset, both from one pan pair panX/panY in [-1,1]; ZOOM via box-sizing #bg (not transform). Exact CSS from Grok (union stage S, zoom z>=1):
  objectPositionX% = (panX+1)/2*100 ; objectPositionY% = (panY+1)/2*100
  left% = 50*(1-z)*(1+panX) ; top% = 50*(1-z)*(1+panY)
  width% = height% = 100*z
At z=1 left=top=0 => pure object-position pan (the chopped-bottom fix). At z>1 both offsets add => a stage-sized window slides over the full cover-scaled source (so Move Left/Right works on a wide union when zoomed). object-fit:cover kept; filter brightness(1.01) kept. z<1 FORBIDDEN (black gutters). z in [1,2] step 0.1; pan in [-1,1] step 0.05.

title: Bounce / ping-pong loop option (seamless, no loop seam)
description: User request (Anoop): a bounce / ping-pong loop so a clip plays forward then backward and never shows a loop seam. TECHNICAL CONSTRAINT: HTML5 <video> cannot play in reverse at runtime (negative playbackRate is not supported in WebKit; JS frame-by-frame reverse is janky and CPU heavy). So bounce must be achieved by PRE-PROCESSING the clip into a boomerang (forward + reversed concatenated into one file), which then loops seamlessly with the existing loop attribute. Implementation: a small ffmpeg helper / flag that takes a source clip and emits a boomerang bg.mp4 (e.g. split, reverse the copy, concat), plus docs. Optionally surface it as a per-video option in the config (ow-aqx.2). Note: boomerang doubles the clip length and file size, and the midpoint (the forward end / reverse start) must be a real frame to avoid a 1-frame stutter.
acceptance_criteria: A documented helper produces a boomerang bg.mp4 that plays forward then backward and loops with no visible seam; optionally selectable per video in config.

title: True WKWebView desktop-through transparency on macOS 26 (public path is opaque)
description: Finding from ow-94b.1: on macOS 26 the public WKWebView transparency path (underPageBackgroundColor=.clear + transparent html/body CSS) does NOT make the base transparent; it renders opaque (an screencapture -l of the window interior comes back opaque, not the black that a truly transparent buffer yields). The de-facto macOS fix is the semi-private KVC setValue(false, forKey: 'drawsBackground'), which the project chose to avoid. For now WebWallpaperView uses an opaque base with a black CSS fallback, and the full-bleed video covers it, so the wallpaper itself is unaffected. This task is only needed when an Epic D overlay/blend effect actually needs the real desktop to show THROUGH the web layer. Then decide: accept the drawsBackground KVC (document the private-API risk), or find a public macOS 26 approach (overriding isOpaque, a transparent CALayer host, an alternate view). Verify with a hollow-interior page: screencapture -D of an uncovered display must show the real desktop through the interior.
acceptance_criteria: Either a public macOS 26 approach yields a genuinely transparent WKWebView base (desktop visible through a hollow page region in a -D display capture), or the drawsBackground KVC is adopted with the private-API risk documented and a fallback if it breaks.

STORAGE/SEED: appSupportRoot() = env OW_APP_SUPPORT_DIR (tests) else ~/Library/Application Support/OnlyWallpapers. seedWebDirIfNeeded(from bundleWebDir) runs ONCE from AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching BEFORE initialBuild() - NEVER from resolve() or performCommit (those run on every hot-plug rebuild; seeding there would rewrite live code under N running views). Seeds appSupport/web/ with index.html+style.css+wallpaper.js ONLY when missing OR CFBundleVersion/content-hash differs; copies the 3 as a unit (web/.seed-tmp -> atomic rename); NEVER touches assets/ (user video persists). Deletes leftover *.partial + replacement dirs on seed (no-growth). Seeds a default bg.mp4 only when the slot is missing AND true-first-run/test.

Log source=env|appstore|bundle. (Widening allowingReadAccessTo cannot work: common ancestor of /Applications and ~/Library is /; co-location is the least-WebKit-surface fix. No WKURLSchemeHandler in v1 - CORS+range+document-serving.)
PICKER: AppDelegate owns WallpaperController+StatusItemController; passes a closure/coordinator to the status item (NO window discovery). 'Choose video...' above Quit. Action (MainActor): picking=true + disable item; NSApp.activate() (Tahoe API, not deprecated activate(ignoringOtherApps:)); DispatchQueue.main.async; NSOpenPanel canChooseFiles, no dirs/multi, allowedContentTypes=[.mpeg4Movie] (v1 MP4-ONLY: a .mov onto bg.mp4 with type=video/mp4 paints black), level>=.modalPanel, directoryURL=Movies; runModal(). On OK: copy off-main via Task.detached/nonisolated helper -> Result to appSupport/web/assets/bg.mp4.partial (SAME dir) then FileManager.replaceItemAt into bg.mp4; check free space; log ONLYWALLPAPERS_VIDEO slot=ok|fail bytes=. Back on MainActor reloadVideo() + re-enable. Picker ALWAYS writes to app storage (never the WALLPAPER_WEB_DIR source tree); in dev (WALLPAPER_WEB_DIR set) disable the item or document. copyInFlight lock prevents re-entry.
RELOAD (preserve ow-blz.3): IN-PLACE JS swap window.__setWallpaperVideo(src) that removes <source> children, sets video.src=assets/bg.mp4?rev=token, load()/play() - NOT webView.reload() (its document-start userscript carries only INIT geometry + does not reset isLoaded -> wrong-slice flash + fights hot-plug). title: Lock-screen poster frame: set a per-display desktop picture so the wallpaper shows when locked
description: The live WKWebView layer cannot render on the macOS secure lock screen (it is a user-session window; the lock surface composites above it - confirmed in ow-aad.1). But the lock screen DOES natively render the system DESKTOP PICTURE. So we can make the wallpaper appear on lock by ALSO setting a static poster frame of the video as the real per-display desktop picture (the same official mechanism multi-monitor wallpaper tools like Fresco use to show on the lock screen). On the active desktop the live animated layer still sits on top (animation unaffected); on lock the live layer is gone and macOS shows the poster. User is happy with a freeze-frame on lock. Not urgent; nice touch.
design:
MECHANISM: NSWorkspace.shared.setDesktopImageURL(url, for: screen, options:) per NSScreen - official API, no private APIs. The desktop picture sits BELOW our desktop-window-level live layer, so setting/refreshing it is invisible on the active desktop and only seen on the lock screen.
CAPTURE: WKWebView.takeSnapshot(config) per WebWallpaperView to grab each display's EXACT rendered slice - this faithfully includes the current video frame + the mood tint filter + framing zoom/pan, so the frozen lock image matches what was on screen. Write each snapshot PNG to app storage and set it as that screen's desktop picture. (Alternative: AVAssetImageGenerator pulls a clean frame from the source mp4 but would miss mood/framing; prefer takeSnapshot for fidelity. Reuse the existing union/slice geometry so each screen gets its own correctly-sliced poster and the bezel stays continuous on lock.)
REFRESH: regenerate the poster on a timer (~2-5 min), on video change (Choose video), on framing/mood change, and ideally just before sleep/lock (observe NSWorkspace sleep / screensDidSleep / the lock notification) so the frozen frame is recent. Note: macOS itself snapshots the desktop picture for the lock screen inconsistently (the user has seen this with Fresco) - we can keep the picture fresh but cannot fully control when macOS re-reads it for the lock screen; document this.
OPT-IN: this CHANGES the system desktop picture (a real side effect), so gate it behind a menu toggle ('Show wallpaper on lock screen') - fold into ow-aqx.7 or a dedicated item.
RESTORE DECISION (important): on quit the last poster frame would remain the user's desktop picture. Decide: either (a) capture the user's ORIGINAL per-display desktop picture on first enable and RESTORE it on quit/disable (cleaner), or (b) accept that the poster (a frame of their own chosen wallpaper) becomes the desktop picture. Recommend (a) with a saved original path.
Relates to ow-aad.1 (lifecycle: wallpaper not drawn on lock).
acceptance_criteria: With the feature enabled, locking the Mac shows a recent still frame of the wallpaper on every display, correctly sliced (bezel-continuous) and matching the on-screen look (video frame + mood tint + framing); the live animation on the desktop is unchanged; the poster refreshes on video/mood/framing change and periodically (and before sleep/lock where observable); enabling is an explicit opt-in (it sets the system desktop picture); a defined behavior for the user's original desktop picture on quit/disable (restore it, or documented).

title: Video playlist: timed cross-fade between multiple wallpapers
description: Point the app at a FOLDER of videos (or a small preloaded set) and have it cycle through them: every N minutes (configurable, default ~30-60 min) it CROSS-FADES from the current video into the next, so the wallpaper itself slowly evolves, not just the single looping clip. The cross-dissolve must be smooth (opacity blend between two stacked video layers), never a hard cut or black flash, and must stay identical and in sync across all displays so the bezel-spanning slice stays continuous. Larger scope / not urgent (user: 'much later, not important right now, just scope it'). Builds on the existing single-video picker (ow-aqx.2).
design:
Two-layer cross-fade: a second video element (e.g. #bg2) stacked on #bg; the ACTIVE layer plays, the NEXT is preloaded/decoding, then an opacity cross-dissolve swaps them. Both layers carry the per-screen slice geometry (left/top on #stage), object-fit:cover, AND the framing (zoom/pan) and mood filter so the look is consistent through the fade (apply framing+mood to a wrapping container, or to both layers identically). NO CSS transform (ow-blz.2: transforms blank the hardware video layer); fade via opacity only, and re-validate the hardware recomposite path (ow-94b.5) with TWO decoding <video>s during the transition window.
SYNC: native is the clock. The controller broadcasts {currentIndex, nextIndex, transitionAtEpoch, durationMs} to every WebWallpaperView (mirror the geometry/framing/mood broadcast) so every screen shows the SAME current+next video and cross-fades at the SAME wall-clock moment. Playlist order resolved natively (sequential or shuffle-no-immediate-repeat).
SOURCE/CONFIG: a 'Choose folder...' menu item (extends the ow-aqx.2 single-slot picker) OR a playlist dir seeded in app-storage; store the folder path, interval, and shuffle flag in config.json (already merge-based since ow-aqx.15, so new keys coexist with framing + weatherCache). Enumerate video files (mp4/h264) from the folder; handle add/remove between cycles.
PERFORMANCE (the user's heat concern, esp. the 2019 Intel MBP at 4K multi-display): a cross-fade decodes TWO videos at once for the transition window -> ~2x decode load spike. Keep only current+next loaded (never the whole folder), keep the cross-fade short (~1-2s), tear down the outgoing layer immediately after, and make the whole playlist pausable/disable-able. Measure media=playing + thermals before/after on real hardware (Phase 5).
INTERACTIONS: framing nudges apply to the active (and incoming) video; the adaptive mood tint (ow-aqx.15) composes over the active video; hot-plug display rebuild must carry the current playlist position so a newcomer screen joins mid-cycle in sync.
acceptance_criteria: A folder of >=2 videos cycles with a smooth opacity cross-fade (no black flash) at a configurable interval; all displays show the same video and fade at the same instant (bezel-continuous); framing + mood still apply through and after the fade; only current+next are ever loaded (no whole-folder memory/thermal blowup); the hardware video stays live (media=playing) across the transition on real multi-display hardware; the playlist can be paused/disabled; config (folder, interval, shuffle) persists in config.json without clobbering framing/weather keys.
notes: TARGET MACHINE (clarified by user): the PRIMARY target is the Mac Mini (Apple Silicon) with MULTIPLE monitors. The 2019 Intel 15in MacBook Pro is SINGLE-screen and NOT a design target - its current capability is the acceptable ceiling ('maximum standard'); do NOT scale back or gate this feature on Intel-MBP thermals. Reframe the performance note in the design accordingly: design/tune for Apple Silicon + multi-monitor; the earlier '2019 Intel MBP at 4K multi-display' heat framing is wrong (the MBP is single-screen and best-effort - the user just quits it if it runs hot). The two-videos-decoding-at-once cost still matters, but judged against the Mac Mini + multi-monitor, not the Intel laptop.

design: Extend the Open-Meteo request with current=wind_speed_10m,wind_direction_10m (plus the existing cloud_cover/precipitation). Particles emitted on the #overlay canvas (aqx.3), velocity = f(wind_speed, wind_direction); density = f(precipitation). Reuse the same cheap particle engine as rain/snow. design: Trigger from the Stage-1 weather signal (storm WMO 95-99). A flash = short opacity ramp on a white/pale overlay element (or a brief brightness filter spike) over ~150-400ms, 1-3 quick blinks, then a long random quiet gap (tens of seconds to minutes) so it reads as distant lightning, not a strobe. title: Transient real-wallpaper reveals during system transitions (widget drag, Space switch)
description: Our desktop-layer window is briefly replaced by the REAL system wallpaper during some system-driven transitions, then our content returns. Two observed instances on macOS 26.5.2 (ow-mbw.1 spike): (1) WIDGET DRAG: while dragging a desktop widget (clock, calendar), the real wallpaper (dimmed) shows in place of our window for the drag duration, returning on drop. (2) FULL-SCREEN TO DESKTOP SPACE SWITCH: navigating (cmd+arrow / swipe) from a full-screen app Space back to the desktop Space, the old/real wallpaper flashes for about a second during the slide animation before our window appears. Same class: the compositor shows the true desktop during the transition and our desktop-level window paints a beat late. Likely related to Mission Control / Space-transition surface snapshotting. Investigate whether either is preventable (window level/flags, reacting to transition notifications); may be inherent system behavior. Belongs with Spaces/lifecycle work (see ow-aad.1). Low priority.
design: Do NOT assume this is unfixable: research what macOS actually does during widget drag (widget-edit mode compositing, whether our desktop-level window can stay visible, any notifications for enter/exit widget-edit, window level/flags options). Candidate fallbacks if the reveal cannot be fully prevented: (1) PREFERRED: on drag/widget-edit start, grab a freeze-frame (thumbnail of the current rendered frame) and show it so the swap looks seamless, restoring live render on drag end; needs a way to detect widget-edit start quickly. (2) LOWER: set the user's actual system wallpaper to solid black so that whatever the OS reveals during widget drag is just black (not an unrelated photo), which looks intentional rather than jarring. Priority stays P3: user rarely drags widgets once placed.
acceptance_criteria: Documented behavior; if avoidable, our window stays visible during widget drag, otherwise the limitation is recorded.
notes: User guidance (Anoop): dig deeper and research, do not assume can/cannot be done. Low priority because widgets are rarely dragged once set.

title: smoke-run policy check relies on app self-report, not an independent query
description: NON-BLOCKING finding from the ow-mbw.2 Phase 3 review. scripts/smoke-run.sh asserts the activation policy from the app's own stdout ready line (ONLYWALLPAPERS_READY policy=accessory). A future hardcoded or drifted ready line could evade it. The static guard (setActivationPolicy called exactly once and is .accessory) plus the Bool precondition reduce the risk, but the runtime assertion is not independent. Options: query the OS classification during the liveness window (e.g. lsappinfo info -only ApplicationType -app <pid> should report UIElement for .accessory), which Phase 5 of ow-mbw.2 did manually. Fold that into the smoke script, or into ow-mbw.4 (window-config assertions + run check).
acceptance_criteria: smoke-run (or ow-mbw.4) verifies the runtime activation policy via an OS-level query independent of the app's own stdout.

title: Overlay canvas hook for future effects
description: Wire the overlay <canvas> sizing and a no-op render loop as a scaffold for particles/clock/reactive effects later.
notes:
SPIKE DONE (throwaway, reverted) - all risks cleared on real 3-monitor hardware:
- Canvas animation RUNS smoothly on the desktop-layer WKWebView: rAF measured 52.6 fps, setInterval 49.6 fps (300 particles + HUDs across 3 displays). rAF is the better choice; the earlier rAF-throttling only affected a ONE-SHOT deferred callback at load, NOT a sustained self-rescheduling loop. Use requestAnimationFrame for the engine.
- Compositing over the live video WORKS, but the canvas must stay TRANSPARENT: clear/trail via globalCompositeOperation='destination-out' (fade toward transparent), NEVER a translucent-black fillRect (that accumulates to opaque and hides the video). Particles/HUD drawn source-over at full opacity.
- Size the overlay BACKING STORE to stageW*dpr x stageH*dpr (CSS size 100%); the existing #overlay is z-index 1 over #bg z-index 0, pointer-events none.
- Video stays media=playing under the overlay on all 3 displays.
PRODUCTION aqx.3 = minimal clean scaffold: size the overlay (+re-size on hot-plug/geometry change), a rAF render loop that is a no-op/inert by default and exposes a register(drawFn) hook for effects, transparent destination-out clear, and an enable/disable so it costs ~0 when no effect is active. Then ow-wgt (lightning) / ow-l9w (rain - basically proven by this spike) build on it.
